Package com.cognizant.emk.multiagent.application.chat

Class ChatRequestBuilder

java.lang.Object
com.cognizant.emk.multiagent.application.chat.ChatRequestBuilder
@Service public class ChatRequestBuilder extends Object
Translates Agent + memory window into a ChatRequest ready for LlmChatClient (US-11-003).

Re-fetches the agent on every call — this is the REQ-AGT-014 load-bearing piece. There is no per-conversation snapshot of the agent configuration; editing the agent (system prompt, sampling, tools, enabled MCPs, team) takes effect on the very next turn.

Defense-in-depth against agent / catalog drift: tool and MCP names on the agent are validated against the static catalogs (loaded once at startup). Unknown names — which the EPIC-07 / EPIC-08 write-time validators forbid — surface as AgentConfigurationDriftException, mapped to 500 by the global handler.

Filesystem MCP per-user scoping (REQ-MCP-005): when the agent has filesystem enabled and the conversation is owned by a ConversationOwner.UserOwner, the per-user root is materialized on demand via FilesystemMcpUserScope.resolveUserRoot(UserId) — a side effect that ensures the directory exists before the LLM call begins streaming. SYSTEM-owned conversations are unreachable in v1 (US-10-005 makes that a deterministic 404), so the SYSTEM dispatch defensively throws.

  • Method Details

    • build

      public ChatRequest build(AgentId agentId, ConversationOwner owner, List<Message> memoryWindow)
      Builds the per-turn ChatRequest.

      The memoryWindow is the chronologically-ASCENDING list of past messages — including the just-persisted USER message at its tail (see MemoryWindowAssembler's Javadoc on the single-query approach).

      Throws:
      AgentNotFoundException - if the agent was deleted mid-turn.
      AgentConfigurationDriftException - if the agent references a tool or MCP server no longer in the catalog.
